result.verdict:
**VERDICT: FAIL.** Fourth consecutive fail, and the first one where no check fired at all. Three unrelated Danish trades — a sewing-machine workshop, a district-heating console, a church-organ workshop — produced three sites on the same near-achromatic mid grey, each named after a metal, each carrying one warm-metal ochre inside a 4.7 degree arc, none carrying an image, all written in one voice. A designer shown these cold would say "these are all on grey" before saying anything else. The round-four checks did not stop it, and the check written specifically to stop it was never wired to a measurement.

---

## 1. The four-round table

Rounds one to three are the published cells. Round four I measured myself off the rendered pages at 1440 in the browser default scheme. My pipeline reproduces every published number exactly (R1 ground 87.7/72.0/70.0 → 17.7; R1 lum spread 0.301; R2 ground 41.1/42.0/37.9 → 4.1; R2 spread 0.387; R3 ground 39.2/40.0/218.6 → 179.4; R3 spread 0.573), so the round-four row is comparable rather than re-derived.

| Measure | Round one | Round two | Round three | **Round four** |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| **Ground hue arc** | 17.7° (87.7/72.0/70.0) | 4.1° (41.1/42.0/37.9) | 179.4° (39.2/40.0/218.6) | **89.4°** (101.5/190.9/160.0) |
| … closest ground pair, perceptual ΔE76 | 7.2 | 1.5 | 26.1 | **2.7** (B vs C, 9 RGB units apart) |
| … ground chroma C\*, per build | 7.3 / 5.2 / 3.1 | 7.0 / 7.6 / 14.2 | 18.8 / 5.4 / 5.4 | **8.0 / 3.4 / 2.5** |
| **Raised-surface hue arc** | 6.2° | 3.0° | 1.9° | **89.8°** (96.9/186.7/120.0) |
| … its chroma C\* | — | — | — | **7.6 / 2.9 / 2.6** |
| **Emphatic accent hue arc** | 30.0° | 31.7° | 143.3° | **151.8°** (9.5/44.2/161.3) |
| … its **saturation band** | 18.6 wide (59.5–78.1%) | 4.5 wide (72.9–77.4%) | 38.7 wide (61.3–100%) | **9.4 wide (70.1–79.5%)** |
| **Signature-material hue arc** | not separated from ground | not separated from ground | 0.8° (39.2/40.0/39.5) | **78.5°** (101.5/180.0/160.0) — but C\* 8.0/2.5/2.5 |
| **Ground luminance spread** | 0.301 | 0.387 | 0.573 | **0.140** ← narrowest of four rounds |
| **Saturated values per build** (S≥38%, L 15–70%) | 1 / 1 / 1 | 4 / 2 / 3 | 2 / 2 / 2 | **2 / 2 / 1** |
| **Shared structural devices, all three** | 1 (hairlines) | 1 (flat-surfaces) | 0 | **0** |
| … worst pair | 2 (B+C) | 2 (A+B) | 1 (A+B) | **2 (A+B: flat-surfaces, tabular figures)** |
| Display faces | 3 distinct | 3 distinct | 3 distinct | 3 distinct (Familjen Grotesk / Zilla Slab / Archivo Narrow) |
| First-screen imagery, best site | 0% | 0% | 10.76% | **0.0%** |
| clip-path + drop-shadow lifted sheet | — | — | 2 of 2 non-console builds | **0 / 0 / 0** |

Round four's grounds, measured: A `rgb(159,168,155)` lum 0.377, B `rgb(183,192,194)` lum 0.517, C `rgb(182,188,186)` lum 0.495.

**The two cells that matter.** The ground and signature arcs look like large widenings and are not. All three round-four grounds sit at CIELAB chroma ≤ 8 — the lowest mean of any round, lower than round one. At that chroma the hue number is noise: a ±2 RGB-unit change swings A's ground hue 9.3°, B's 10.9° and C's **20.0°**. B's ground and C's ground are **9 RGB units apart** — inside the repository's own 12-unit "this is the same colour" threshold in `gate.mjs` — and the ledger records them as hue 190.9 and *achromatic*. The 89.4° arc is measured between three greys. The honest cell is the ΔE row: **26.1 → 2.7**, a 90 percent collapse, the tightest ground pair since round two.

---

## 2. Did the checks fire, and did the builds obey the purpose or the letter?

**No check fired. Zero refusals, across all three builds, across every convergence check in the package.** Verbatim from the reports:

- A, `PRODUCTION-REPORT.md`: `ledger: 0 poster før denne kørsel / verdict: passed, this shape is not in the ledger`; "hver kontrol kørte og ingen nægtede."
- B, mechanical findings: "`ledger/anti-repeat`: ingen. **Ingen veto mod fingerprint, ground-, accent- eller signaturkulør.**" and "`gate/palette-and-typeface`: ingen."
- C: "**Ingen af de fire skærpede kontroller i denne runde afviste noget**: hverken paletten inden for 12 RGB enheder af premium mønstret, de to display antikvaer og den ene standard grotesk ved navn, det mættede lilla felt, eller hovedbogens bue for grund, accent og signaturmateriale."

Every refusal in round four was hygiene, not convergence: B's incomplete Type section, B's 27 duplicate accessible names, B's 8px target gap, C's broken `Built:` reason clause, C's +20px overflow at 768, two missing-report refusals.

**No build moved a value just past an arc.** Nobody was refused, so nobody re-chose. I checked the margins anyway: the closest anything came to firing was B's ink `#0b171a`, 16.2 RGB units from the banned `#1a1714` against a 12-unit threshold. Nothing suggests gaming.

**The letter/purpose failure is worse than a nudge, and it is in the code.**

**(a) The signature-material veto is dead code. It cannot fire, ever.** `ledger.mjs:294` reads `signatureHue: raw.signatureHue ?? null`. `raw.signatureHue` is **never assigned anywhere in the file**. The `check`/`commit` path sets only:

```js
raw.groundHue = hueOf(raw.groundColor)      // ledger.mjs:685
raw.accentHue = hueOf(raw.accentColor)      // ledger.mjs:686
```

and `measure()` never returns a signature colour. So `signatureHue` is null for every build forever, `hueGap(null, null)` returns null, and line 392 `continue`s past it. All three committed entries in `docs/rebuild/s14/ledger/renders.jsonl` carry `"signatureHue":null`. The veto list and `SIGNATURE_ARC = 30` were written; the measurement was not. Its unit test at `skills/sitesmith-v3/scripts/test-ledger.mjs:187` passes because it injects `signatureHue` directly into `judge()`, bypassing the measurement path — **a green test over a field nothing produces**. Round four's headline fix does not exist in the running system.

**(b) The ground veto goes blind on grey.** `hueOf` returns null below 0.04 chroma. C's ground is chroma 0.0235 → null → never compared to anything. The round-three recommendation *did* land correctly — `ledger.mjs:397-398` now only widens the arc across luminance bands instead of skipping the comparison — but it was moot, because no two grounds were within 25° of each other on the hue the ledger could see. The two grounds that are in fact the same colour were the two the check could not reach.

That is the letter defeating the purpose, and it did not require a build to game anything: **all three landed in the region where the arc is not defined.** I have no evidence of intent — the direction records say the colours came from the trade's materials before anything was run, and C's report states it explicitly. The effect is the same either way. A hue veto pushed three builds out of hue.

**(c) The repository's own tool has the same hole.** `portfolio-diversity.mjs` pre-splits `groundFamily` at luminance 0.5 and at |r−b| = 6. B (0.517) and C (0.495) are 0.022 apart and land in different halves; B's r−b of −11 crosses the warm/cool line by 5 units. So the tool reports a two-site problem and misses that all three grounds are inside 0.140 luminance — comfortably inside its own declared `groundBand` of 0.18.

---

## 3. Where the convergence is now

I checked every candidate against `skills/sitesmith-v3/SKILL.md`, `run.md`, `gate.mjs` and `ledger.mjs` before counting it. Things the package names are **not** evidence, and round four reproduces all of them: naming the signature's kind, the horizontal gauge as the kind to reject (SKILL.md 137–141), cutting `01/02/03`, "let the count fall out", "not a list of roles", "spend your boldness in one place", the autopilot block, arguing the runner-up, the two swaps. Note also that the three autopilot descriptions agreeing on *mono uppercase labels* and *a three-card grid* does **not** count this round: `ledger.mjs`'s seed recipe names `mono-uppercase-labels` verbatim and `gate.mjs` refuses the three-card grid, so all three builders were told those are the tells. Round three counted that; it should not have.

What nothing forced:

**1. The ochre triple — 4.7 degrees, and it is round three's tell wearing new nouns.** Every build contains exactly one warm metal ochre, and they are the same colour:

| build | token | material | hex | hue | sat |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| A | `--olie` | oil film on a freshly polished frame | `#d69a26` | **39.5°** | 69.8% |
| B | `--messing` | the brass nipple in a heating plant | `#c99a17` | **44.2°** | 79.5% |
| C | `--egetræ` | the oak of the wind chest | `#7d6a3f` | **41.6°** | 33.0% |

Round three's signature-material tell sat at 39.2 / 40.0 / 39.5. **Round four's ochre triple sits at 39.5 / 44.2 / 41.6 — the same region.** The material changed (manila card → oil film, reading sheet → brass, tawed sheepskin → oak); the hue did not. All three render (3, 4 and 2 uses respectively). And the ledger cannot see it, because its accent rule takes only the *single most saturated* colour per build: A's ochre lost to a rust-red thread by 4.1 saturation points, C's oak falls below the 0.35 saturation gate, so of the three ochres exactly one entered the fingerprint. The ledger compared 10 / 44 / 161 and saw a wide family. The pages contain 39.5 / 44.2 / 41.6.

**2. All three pages are a sheet of grey metal, and the luminance spread is the narrowest of four rounds.** `--maskinlak` (lacquer over cast iron), `--zink` (galvanised insulation plate), `--pibemetal` (tin-lead pipe metal). Chroma 8.0 / 3.4 / 2.5, luminance 0.377 / 0.517 / 0.495, spread **0.140** — narrower than round one's 0.301. Nobody chose paper, nobody chose white, nobody chose dark. Round three had a light cream at 0.85 and a mid-dark at 0.277; both are gone. Nothing in the package says grey, metal or mid-tone. This is round three's signature tell promoted one level up: instead of three signatures cut from one colour, three *whole pages* cut from one material.

**3. All three spend their one named risk on the same sentence.** §6 asks for one risk and does not say which axis. All three chose the ground, against the category:
- A: "Bunden er maskinlak i mellemtone og der er intet hvidt felt på siden. Kategorien sætter altid brugt maskineri på hvidt eller råhvidt papir."
- B: "En lys zinkflade til en driftskonsol, uden en eneste rød farve… Kategorien ville lave den mørk med grøn, gul og rød."
- C: "The ground is a mid grey metal sheet, not paper and not white. A church trade page that refuses warmth is the thing the category never does."

Three-way agreement in the risk slot, in one voice. This is round two's finding — the tell moving onto the fix — reappearing on a new field.

**4. Imagery is zero in all three, and this is a regression.** First-screen asset share 0.0 / 0.0 / 0.0. Round three's C carried 10.76 percent. The portfolio tool has now failed imagery four rounds running.

**5. The voice has not moved since round one.** Short declarative Danish, present tense, and every build still closes on what it refuses to claim — now as a named section in all three: A's "Det du ikke finder her", C's "Elektroniske orgler laver vi ikke", B's "Intet er sendt fra denne skærm endnu… Skærmen styrer ikke anlægget, den ser på det og sender folk ud." A paragraph still moves between the three unnoticed.

**What genuinely died, and it is real.** Round three's clip-path-plus-drop-shadow lifted sheet is gone (0 clip-paths, 0 drop-shadow filters, all three). Round three's shared signature kind is gone: round four produced a specimen (A's stitch row), a dimensioned cross-section document (B's 61 pipe-pair sections) and a worn struck surface (C's stamp) — three of the seven kinds, three different ones. The raised-surface arc, which had tightened monotonically 6.2 → 3.0 → 1.9 across three rounds, broke to 89.8. The "everyone counted to exactly two saturated values" tell broke (2/2/1). Shared ledger devices stayed at 0. Six typefaces, no overlap.

---

## 4. Render

**Rendered, not read.** Playwright/Chromium via the MCP browser tools, served from `docs/rebuild/` on 127.0.0.1:8114. 1440×900 viewport plus full-page for A, B and C; 375×812 for A, B and C. Six renders, all three builds at both widths, plus three separate headless measurement passes (round-four colour extraction, four-round ground chroma, four-round device counts) and one headless pass over s11/s12/s13 to confirm my pipeline reproduces the published cells. ## Is the structural approach working, or does one skill produce a family resemblance no check can remove?

**The structural approach is working, and round four is not a test of it, because round four did not run the check it claims to have run.** The four-round trend is unambiguous once you separate the axes that had a working check from the axes that did not: round three's single fired veto moved a value 143 degrees, changed the noun, forced a contrast re-measure and produced every widening in that round — that is not a model nudging past a threshold, that is the mechanism doing exactly what it was designed to do; and in round four the two axes that kept a live check (accent hue, devices) held at 151.8° and 0 shared devices, while the two axes whose check was unreachable collapsed to the tightest values in the study, ΔE 2.7 on the ground and 4.7° on the ochre. The signature-material veto — the fix this entire round was built around — is a field that no code path ever assigns, guarded by a unit test that injects the value by hand, so the round labelled "the first with all of it live" ran with one of three tightened checks structurally incapable of firing and a second one blinded by a 0.04 chroma floor that all three builds happened to slip under. Three rounds of relocation is exactly what a veto that names one closed region should produce — the model has the entire rest of the space and will use it — but relocation at 143 degrees is a mechanism working, not a resemblance that cannot be removed. What would change my mind: a round in which every check is verified to fire on the pages themselves — `signatureHue` actually measured off the rendered signature element, and hue proximity replaced by a perceptual floor (ΔE or a chroma-aware distance) so that two greys 9 RGB units apart cannot pass a colour veto by having no hue — and the convergence still reappears somewhere new at the same tightness. If it does, the tell is in the process. Until that round is run, every piece of evidence you have is about coverage.
